title: Hematopoietic cell lineages
alt: Original scholarly lineage tree with erythrocyte and macrophage artwork.
alterations: Original preserved. Film uses resized/cropped lineage, erythrocyte and macrophage images; reversible cell deformation, production, clearance and schematic transport markers added.

title: Normal vessel repair and hemostasis
credit: OpenStax College, Anatomy and Physiology (2013), 1909 Blood Clotting; part (a) credit Kevin MacKenzie
alt: Original hemostasis figure, including the vessel cross-section used as a reference in the films.
alterations: Original preserved. The vessel segment is cropped/rescaled. Schematic cell motion, intravascular fibrin accumulation, impaired flow and consumption markers are added; DIC overlays are distinguished from the original normal-repair figure.

title: Sickle erythrocyte
credit: Database Center for Life Science (DBCLS), Togo picture gallery (2024), DOI 10.7875/togopic.2024.219
alt: Original DBCLS illustration of sickle erythrocytes.
alterations: Original SVG preserved. Rendered to sickle.png with CairoSVG, then cell crop/rescale and schematic motion added.
licenseNote: Commons review is pending; the DBCLS institutional announcement independently states CC BY 4.0 for TogoTV illustrations.

title: Internal anatomy of the heart
alt: Original OpenStax anterior heart cutaway with chambers, valves and vessels labeled.
alterations: Original preserved. Film uses an anatomical crop/rescale, schematic flow markers and valve-state marks, and relative volume markers. Posterior aortic flow is hidden where the anterior pulmonary trunk overlies it. No image generation or invented organ anatomy.

title: Normal heart and ventricular septal defect
credit: CDC, National Center on Birth Defects and Developmental Disabilities
license: U.S. public domain, absent a stated third-party copyright restriction
alt: CDC comparison of a normal heart and VSD, with an arrow crossing the ventricular septum.
alterations: Original preserved. Film crops/rescales the paired anatomy and adds schematic left-to-right and pulmonary flow. Use does not imply endorsement by CDC, HHS, or the U.S. Government.
